**Refined prompt:** Why can users no longer log in after changing their password? I'm answering as a security-minded engineer tracing the password write path. The answer comes first, then cited evidence.

Changing a password saves it as plain text, and login can only check hashed passwords. So the check fails every time.

**Evidence**

1. Hashing only runs on insert. `src/user/user.entity.ts:28-31`:
   ```ts
   @BeforeInsert()
   async hashPassword() {
     this.password = await argon2.hash(this.password);
   ```
   It does not run when an existing user is saved.

2. The update path never hashes. `src/user/user.service.ts:74-80`:
   ```ts
   let toUpdate = await this.userRepository.findOne(id);
   delete toUpdate.password;
   delete toUpdate.favorites;

   let updated = Object.assign(toUpdate, dto);
   return await this.userRepository.save(updated);
   ```
   The `delete toUpdate.password` line removes the old hash. `Object.assign` then copies the request body onto the entity. If the body has a `password`, the plain text goes to the database.

3. Nothing filters the body. `src/user/user.controller.ts:26-28` has no `@UsePipes(new ValidationPipe())` on `PUT user`. The `@UsePipes` lines at 31 and 42 cover only `POST users` and `POST users/login`. A TypeScript DTO type does not remove fields at runtime, so a `password` in the body passes through.

4. Login then fails. `src/user/user.service.ts:31`: `if (await argon2.verify(user.password, password))`. The stored value is now plain text, not an argon2 hash, so the check fails. `findOne` returns `null`, and the controller returns 401 (`user.controller.ts:48`).

**Fix:**
- In `UserService.update()`, stop merging the body with `Object.assign`.
- Copy the allowed fields by name: `username`, `email`, `bio`, `image`.
- If `password` is present, set `toUpdate.password = await argon2.hash(dto.password)`.

**Not read:**
- `src/user/dto/update-user.dto.ts`. I did not open it, so I don't know whether it declares `password`.
- The running database. I did not confirm that affected rows hold plain text.
- Other write paths. I only grepped `src/user`, so I can't rule out another place that writes a password.

**Side effects to decide on:** the `Object.assign` also lets a client change `id` or `email` through the same route. Users who already changed their password are locked out. Their rows hold plain text, so they need a reset or a one-off rehash. I haven't changed any code. Do you want me to make the fix?

Likely category: security — Auth / permission question: trace the enforcement point and assume the caller is hostile.

### [CURRENT_FOCUS.md] CURRENT_FOCUS.md > CURRENT FOCUS — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Active now
- [ ] **Spec conformance pass** — make article responses match the RealWorld spec: produce
      `favorited` per current user, rename `favoriteCount` → `favoritesCount` and
      `created/updated` → `createdAt/updatedAt` at the response boundary (not in the DB).
- [ ] **Ownership checks** on `PUT/DELETE /articles/:slug` and `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id`
      — return 403 when the caller is not the author. Design first; the comment case needs a
      `comment.author` relation that does not exist yet.
- [ ] **Password change path** — hash on update (see LESSONS.md #88) and stop the raw body
      being merged into the entity.

### [CURRENT_FOCUS.md] CURRENT_FOCUS.md > CURRENT FOCUS — RealWorld API (NestJS)
> Living doc. What is actually in flight right now. Read after LESSONS.md.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A lifecycle hook that hashes on insert does not run on update (#88)
**What happened:** `PUT /user` with `{ "user": { "password": "newpassword" } }` wrote the string
`newpassword` into the `password` column. `UserEntity.hashPassword()` is `@BeforeInsert()` only;
`UserService.update()` does `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)` and saves, so the plaintext went
straight to MySQL. Users who changed their password could never log in again — `argon2.verify`
compares the typed password against a non-hash and fails.

**Rule:** every write path a secret can travel must hash it explicitly, and `@BeforeInsert`
covers exactly one of them. When you see a hook, ask which lifecycle events it does NOT cover.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Every handler returns the RO envelope, never a bare entity (#57)
**What happened:** `ArticleController.create()` returned `ArticleEntity` directly while every
other handler returns `{ article }`. The React frontend read `response.article.slug` → `Cannot
read property 'slug' of undefined` right after creating an article. The server logged nothing —
from its side the request succeeded.

**Rule:** the envelope (`ArticleRO`, `UserRO`, …) is the contract with every RealWorld client.
A handler whose return type is not a `*RO` interface is a bug even if it "works" in Postman.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Passwords
- Hashed by `UserEntity.hashPassword()` under `@BeforeInsert()` only.
- `UserService.update()` does `delete toUpdate.password` then `Object.assign(toUpdate, dto)`
  and saves. `UpdateUserDto` declares no `password` field, but nothing strips one from the
  request body, and `PUT /user` has no validation pipe.
- Login: `UserService.findOne({email, password})` → `argon2.verify(hash, password)`; unknown
  email or wrong password both return `null` → controller throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)`.
- Registration duplicate → `400` with `{ message: 'Input data validation failed', errors }`.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > DTOs
Plain classes in `dto/`, `readonly` fields. Only `CreateUserDto` carries `class-validator`
decorators (`@IsNotEmpty`); `UpdateUserDto`, `CreateArticleDto`, `CreateCommentDto` have none.
The custom `ValidationPipe` is applied **per handler** with `@UsePipes(new ValidationPipe())`
— it is not global. Today only `POST /users` and `POST /users/login` use it.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`)
Tables are generated from the entity classes at boot. There are no migration files; a column
change is an entity change.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > The token
- Issued by `UserService.generateJWT(user)` (`src/user/user.service.ts`): payload
  `{ id, username, email, exp }`, signed with `SECRET` from `src/config.ts`, **expiry 60 days**.
- Returned inside the `UserRO` envelope on `POST /users` (register), `POST /users/login`, and
  `GET /user`.
- Sent by clients as `Authorization: Token <jwt>` (RealWorld convention). The code only ever
  reads `header.split(' ')[1]`, so `Bearer <jwt>` works too — the scheme word is ignored.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Which routes are guarded (from the three `configure()` blocks)
| Module | Guarded routes (401 without token) |
|---|---|
| `UserModule` | `GET /user`, `PUT /user` |
| `ArticleModule` | `GET /articles/feed` · `POST /articles` · `PUT /articles/:slug` · `DELETE /articles/:slug` · `POST /articles/:slug/comments` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` · `POST /articles/:slug/favorite` · `DELETE /articles/:slug/favorite` |
| `ProfileModule` | `profiles/:username/follow` for **all** methods (POST follow, DELETE unfollow) |

Everything else is **public**: `GET /articles`, `GET /articles/:slug`,
`GET /articles/:slug/comments`, `GET /profiles/:username`, `GET /tags`, `POST /users`,
`POST /users/login`, and — notably — **`DELETE /users/:slug`**, which deletes the user whose
*email* equals the `:slug` param (`UserService.delete(email)`), with no token required and no
check of who is asking.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Static routes are declared before parameterised ones (#7)
**What happened:** `GET /articles/feed` was declared *after* `GET /articles/:slug`, so Nest
matched `feed` as a slug and the feed endpoint returned `{ article: undefined }`. Fixed by moving
`getFeed()` above `findOne()` in `ArticleController`.

**Rule:** in a controller, any literal path (`feed`, `popular`, `search`) goes above the `:slug`
handler. Order in the class is match order.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > A relation that is not eager is `undefined`, not `[]`
**What happened:** `ArticleService.favorite()` loads the user with `findOne(id)` and then calls
`user.favorites.findIndex(...)`. `favorites` is a non-eager `@ManyToMany`, so it is `undefined`
→ `TypeError: Cannot read property 'findIndex' of undefined` → 500 on
`POST /articles/:slug/favorite`. Same pattern in `findAll()` for `?favorited=` (`author.favorites.map`).

**Rule:** before touching `entity.relation` in a service, find the `relations: [...]` or the
`eager: true` that loads it. If neither exists, the property is `undefined`.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Conventions (these are the rules, not suggestions) > Layer order
`controller → service → repository/entity`. Controllers do no business logic and never touch a
repository; services do. Cross-module data (e.g. the article service needs users and follows)
is reached by injecting that module's repository via `TypeOrmModule.forFeature([...])` in the
importing module — see `article.module.ts`.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Authentication is not authorization (#6, #44)
**What happened:** any logged-in user could `PUT` or `DELETE` any other user's article. The
route is in `AuthMiddleware`'s list, so people assumed it was "protected" — but the middleware
only proves the caller is *a* user, and `ArticleService.update()/delete()` never compare
`req.user.id` with `article.author.id`. The Swagger `403 Forbidden` annotations on those handlers
describe a check that does not exist.

**Rule:** for every mutating route, name the line that compares the caller with the record's
owner. If you cannot, there is no ownership check, whatever the decorators say.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Two ways a request learns who the user is > 1. `AuthMiddleware` — `src/user/auth.middleware.ts` (the guard)
Applied **per route, per module**, in each module's `configure(consumer)`. Behaviour:
- no `Authorization` header, or nothing after the space → `HttpException('Not authorized.', 401)`
- header present → `jwt.verify(token, SECRET)` → `userService.findById(decoded.id)` → sets
  `req.user = user.user` and calls `next()`.
- `jwt.verify` **throws** on an expired, malformed or wrongly-signed token, and nothing in the
  middleware catches it — the framework turns that into a **500**, not a 401 (see `LESSONS.md`).
- `findById` throws `HttpException({errors}, 401)` if the id no longer exists.

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > What it is
A backend implementing the [RealWorld](https://github.com/gothinkster/realworld) API spec
(Medium clone: users, profiles, articles, comments, tags, favourites, follows). Any RealWorld
frontend (React, Vue, Angular…) is expected to work against it unchanged — **spec conformance
is the contract**, not just "it works with our own client".

Pinned at upstream commit `c1c2cc4` of `lujakob/nestjs-realworld-example-app` (2021-01-18).

### [.claude/knowledge/workspace.md] workspace.md > RealWorld API (NestJS) — workspace overview > Stack
| Layer | Choice |
|---|---|
| Framework | NestJS 7 (`@nestjs/common` ^7.0.5) |
| ORM | TypeORM 0.2.24, `synchronize: true` (tables are created from entities on boot — there are NO migration files) |
| Database | MySQL (`ormconfig.json`) |
| Auth | JSON Web Token via `jsonwebtoken`, secret in `src/config.ts` (copied from `config.ts.example`) |
| Password hashing | `argon2` |
| Validation | `class-validator` + a hand-written `ValidationPipe` in `src/shared/pipes/validation.pipe.ts` |
| API docs | Swagger at `/docs` |
| Tests | Jest (`jest.json`); only `src/tag/tag.controller.spec.ts` exists |

Global prefix is `api` (`src/main.ts` → `app.setGlobalPrefix('api')`), so every route below is
really `/api/...`. Server listens on 3000.

### [LESSONS.md] LESSONS.md > Lessons Learned — RealWorld API (NestJS) > Never `Object.assign` a request body onto a persisted entity (#112)
**What happened:** `UserService.update()` and `ArticleService.update()` both merge the raw body
into the loaded entity. Any extra field the client sends — `id`, `password`, `authorId`,
`favoriteCount` — is persisted. The DTO type is a TypeScript annotation; it strips nothing at
runtime, and `PUT /user` / `PUT /articles/:slug` have no validation pipe.

**Rule:** copy the allowed fields by name, or whitelist with a validation pipe
(`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true`). The DTO class is not a filter.

### [.claude/knowledge/auth.md] auth.md > Authentication and authorization > Authorization (ownership) — where it is enforced
**Nowhere.** The middleware answers "is this a valid user"; no service or controller method
compares the caller with the record's owner:

| Action | Ownership check |
|---|---|
| `PUT /articles/:slug` | none — `ArticleService.update(slug, body)` does `Object.assign(article, body)` and saves |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug` | none — `delete({slug})` |
| `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` | none — and comments have no author to compare against anyway |
| `DELETE /users/:slug` | none, and unguarded |
| `PUT /user` | implicitly the caller (`@User('id')`), fine |

The Swagger `@ApiResponse({ status: 403 })` lines on the article controller describe an
intended behaviour, not an implemented one — nothing returns 403.

### [.claude/knowledge/schema.md] schema.md > Data model (TypeORM entities, `synchronize: true`) > `comment` — `src/article/comment.entity.ts`
| column | type |
|---|---|
| id | int PK |
| body | varchar |
| articleId | FK → article |

**There is no author column and no relation to `user`.** The RealWorld spec's comment object
has `author`; this entity cannot produce it. `addComment()` sets only `body`.
</workspace_context>
